leverage_rationale: WebMCP is tightly integrated with the safety boundary: the tool registry changes with load validity, and export is intentionally absent until a legal load passes. This is a high-value use of state-dependent tool exposure, although the live test only loaded a sample and did not check it.
leverage_evidence: Pitch specifies commit/export tool absence on failed loads and appearance only after passing.
Live UI visibly includes a tool registry and a load-gating workflow.
execution_rationale: The live app loaded a six-material manifest and enabled checking, with the claimed pre-check state visible. The decisive legal refusal/pass and export transitions were not submitted during observation.
execution_evidence: Sample lab pack populated the manifest and enabled Check this load.
After screenshot showed six line items and NO LOAD CHECKED.
Visible registry showed 0 of 5 tools before checking.
impact_rationale: Correctly preventing unsafe hazardous-material shipping paperwork and surfacing exact regulatory reasons has substantial safety and compliance value.
impact_evidence: Pitch targets 49 CFR segregation and blocks shipping-paper export until a load passes.
Video transcript describes refusal of sulfuric acid/calcium hypochlorite and conditional export.
creativity_rationale: The design makes tool availability itself encode a safety invariant and handles forbidden materials that a UN-keyed index could miss.
creativity_evidence: State-dependent getTools behavior is central to the design.
Submission highlights 256 forbidden materials and handler re-derivation from bytes.
s2_notes: Exceptional WebMCP safety mechanism; live observation verified the manifest gate but not the final check/export state.
advance_reason: High-leverage safety workflow is coherent and substantially supported by live UI plus a detailed demo video.
